accuracy.evidence: Each of the five words is defined the way the DfE Relationships Education guidance and CASEL relationship-skills strand use them: cooperate as working together toward one shared goal, compromise as each side giving up part of what it wants, listen as eyes, waiting and saying back, disagree kindly as respectful words about the idea not the person, and include as inviting someone left out. EYFS ELG Building Relationships wording on working and playing cooperatively is quoted in the adult text.

misconceptions.evidence: Tackles the slips adults see in five-to-eight-year-olds: thinking compromise means one child simply gives in (plan step rejects the all-mine and all-yours cards, givein tag), mistaking quiet for listening while fiddling with a toy (toy and watch tags), treating disagreement as rude or as sulking (rude and sulk tags), and assuming a lone child wants to be left alone (nobody and away tags).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagteam is built on a shared log that only lifts when Fox and Bear are dragged to opposite ends, a plan-card table where the winning card holds half of each wish, a listening-signs hunt, a kind/unkind sorter for disagreement lines and a team circle Duck and Mouse are dragged into. None of the existing personal and social labs (flagshare, flagentry, flagask) uses a joint lift or half-and-half plan cards, and the shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child feels cooperation when the log refuses to rise with one animal and lifts with two, sees compromise as a card that literally contains part of each wish, and finds the five listening signs on Bear's face and hands before naming them. Kind disagreement is learned by sorting real sentences, and inclusion by physically moving the lonely animals into the circle and watching the team grow.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions each have a tempting wrong answer: whether Fox can lift the big log on his own, whether compromise means one friend gets their way, and whether include means leaving Duck to play alone. The log that will not move, the rejected one-sided plan card and Duck smiling inside the circle each disprove the tempting option before the step ends.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions cover all five words, and ten tagged wrong-answer explanations (comp, incl, givein, nobody, over, toy, rude, sulk, watch, away) say why that particular choice misses, for example that talking over a friend stops you hearing them, rather than a generic try again. A streak counter rewards a run of correct answers.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs score about grade 1 on Flesch-Kincaid with short sentences and one new word at a time, each tied to a picture or scene. Adult paragraphs sit near grade 9 and name the DfE, EYFS and CASEL terms. Lab prompts are one short instruction, and every card carries an emoji plus a two or three word label.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph either defines one of the five words with a concrete scene, lists the curriculum terms, names typical mistakes or explains what each lab step practises. The family tip gives a single dinner-table game. Practice and mastery items each test one word in a small story rather than recalling the definition text.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 light and Android dark show the log, plan cards, listening spots (now with short labels under each icon) and team circle inside the canvas with large 'young' buttons. Every drag has a button twin in the control row, and the browser gate completed each Show me within the time limit on the iPhone 13 profile.

accessibility.evidence: axe-core reported no violations in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13. The canvas aria-label is updated with every say() message, so screen readers hear each result. All actions are reachable through labelled buttons, and colour is never the only cue because red and blue wishes also carry dot emojis and words.

sources: DfE (2019, updated 2021) Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education: statutory guidance (caring friendships, respectful relationships)
DfE (2023) Statutory framework for the early years foundation stage: ELG Building Relationships
CASEL (2020) CASEL's SEL Framework: Relationship Skills (communicating clearly, listening actively, cooperating, resolving conflicts constructively)
